utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are a few matters we would like to deal with before we start hearing the testimony of the witness. First, the representative of the Registry has assigned the numbers to the Clark exhibits which were admitted ranging from P2270 up to and including P2337. That's one issue. Now, from yesterday there are still associated exhibits remaining to be tendered, Mr. Jeremy, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. There are 19 remaining associated exhibits from this witness that I originally intended to tender and which are not -- yet been admitted. Your Honours, perhaps we should go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into closed session. Private session would do, I take it otherwise we have to wait for the curtains.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber will now deal with two outstanding matters related to the witness Reynaud Theunens. The Defence notice, objection, and motion to bar Witness Theunens from testifying as an expert filed on the 9th of September, 2013, and the Prosecution's urgent request for pre-assignment of exhibit numbers to the Theunens documents filed on the 23rd of September of this year. On the 8th of January the Prosecution filed its notice of disclosure of Theunens's CV and his expert report. On the 24th of January, the Chamber requested the Prosecution to correct a number of technical mistakes in the uploading of the report, to explain the relevance of certain sections of the report, and to review the report with a view to redact any possible overlap with adjudicated facts. The Prosecution dealt with these matters through its filings of the 14th of February, the 15th of July, and the 26th of July. On the 9th of September, the Defence filed its notice, objection, and motion to bar Witness Theunens from testifying as an expert. The Prosecution has not responded to this submission. As for the applicable law concerning expert evidence, the Chamber refers to its decision concerning Richard Butler filed on the 19th of October, 2012. The Defence argues that Witness Theunens is not an expert and should therefore not be allowed to present expert evidence before the Chamber. The Chamber notes that Theunens's CV sets out that he was educated at the Royal Military Academy in Brussels and that during the last 20 years he has researched and analysed political and military issues, in particular in the former Yugoslavia. Between 2001 and 2008, Theunens worked as an intelligence analyst in the military analysis team at the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal. In this capacity, he drafted a number of reports on armed forces in the former Yugoslavia which were used in other cases before the Tribunal. The Chamber is satisfied that Theunens is a military expert who can assist the Chamber on matters related to the VRS. As for the relevance of part I of the report, covering around 180 pages and dealing with the SFRY armed forces, the Defence argues that this part refers exclusively to facts that fall outside the temporal scope of the indictment. The Defence acknowledges that there will inevitably be a need for references in the report to matters outside the indictment period; however, it argues that the report expands on irrelevant issues that could have been dealt with by precise explanations or footnotes rather than with extensive sections of dense information. In its submission of the 26th of July, 2013, the Prosecution argues that parts I and II of the report are inextricably intertwined and necessary to understand one another. More precisely, the Prosecution refers to a sentence in the executive summary of the report stating that the command and control in the VRS was based on the same principles that applied to the SFRY armed forces and submits that these principles are set out in part I of the report. Having considered the parties' submissions on this matter, the Chamber agrees with the Defence that part I, which is approximately 180 pages long and deals with a matter which appears to be of limited relevance to the indictment, is excessive in length. The Chamber defers its decision on admission of the report; however, the Prosecution is hereby informed that the Chamber is inclined to deny admission of part I and that it should elicit any relevant matters related to this part during the examination of Mr. Theunens. As for any other arguments related to the content and methodology of the Theunens report and about the impartiality or independence of Theunens as a former employee of the Office of the Prosecution, the Chamber considers that this can and should be addressed during the examination of the witness. Finally, with regard to the Defence request to cross-examine the witness, the Chamber notes that he will be called to testify and the Defence will therefore have the opportunity to cross-examine him. Based on the foregoing, the Chamber decides that Witness Theunens may testify as an expert witness and denies the Defence request to bar the Prosecution from presenting his evidence. This concludes the Chamber decision on the Defence notice, objection, and motion to bar Witness Theunens from testifying. The second matter that the Chamber will deal with is the Prosecution's urgent request for pre-assignment of exhibit numbers to the Theunens documents. This request pre-supposes that the Prosecution will tender more than 900 documents with this witness. This is, in the Prosecution's own estimation, more than half of the documents underlying the Theunens report. The Prosecution's request appears to completely ignore the Chamber's guidance on the tendering of underlying material for expert reports delivered on the 29th of October, 2012. In this respect, the parties are referred to transcript pages 4138 and 4139. According to the guidance, the Chamber expects the calling party not to tender such material just because a proposed expert referred to or used the documents in compiling his or her report. The Prosecution is instructed to reconsider its approach for the upcoming Witness Theunens in light of this guidance. The request for pre-assigning exhibit numbers is denied. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 26th of September, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of September, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.15 p.m.,
